solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruler knocked back a drink with a piece of meat

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here the string of pieces is also turned round end to end

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer
ham is a cut of meat from a pig's leg

explanation.surface: A ruler downs a drink while eating some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses A JAR A HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian prince who ruled a state was given this title.

clue.text: Little piece by Tallis wanting content for works

parts.note: a mote is a tiny speck or particle

indicators.note: Tallis without its inside letters keeps only its first and last

explanation.surface: A short composition by the Tudor composer Thomas Tallis is missing material for his works.
explanation.walkthrough: Tallis really wrote these, so the surface hides the definition in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: These are choral compositions, so they are musical works.

clue.text: Man, pretentious or friendly?

parts.note: he stands for a male person
arty means affecting artistic taste

explanation.surface: Is this man showy or just genial?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a warm, cordial welcome is a friendly one.

clue.text: Food from queen breaking eggs with a lot of strength

indicators.note: the queen breaks into the eggs, sitting inside them

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a forte is a strong point

explanation.surface: A dish made from a monarch cracking eggs with great force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims FORTE to FORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A French blue cheese, which is a food.

clue.text: Where people save reefer jacket for aristocratic noble

parts.note: a reefer is a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint

indicators.note: the outer letters form a jacket wrapped round the word aristocratic

parts.note: a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Somewhere people keep a reefer jacket made for an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reefer jacket' reads as one garment, but splits: reefer is one piece, jacket the outside-letters signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account held by two or more people, where they keep savings together.

clue.text: Feverish, eating old tropical root

indicators.note: the word for feverish swallows the letter for old

parts.note: manic means frenzied or feverish

explanation.surface: Someone feverish chewing an aged root from the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for cassava, a starchy tuber grown in hot climates.

clue.text: Palm wrapped in threadbare cambric

indicators.note: the letters are wrapped up inside the words threadbare cambric

explanation.surface: A palm tree swathed in worn-out linen fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This genus includes the betel-nut palm.

clue.text: Motto of procrastinator who's obsessed by image?

definitions.meaning: split as three words, it is what a person who keeps putting things off says
a worshipper of idols is devoted to graven images

explanation.surface: The motto of a time-waster who cares only about appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into I DO LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships idols, that is images, rather than a deity.

clue.text: Avoiding relations in populous area without a lot of hurry

indicators.note: in the old sense outside: the city surrounds the hurry

parts.note: a city is a densely populated place

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: haste is hurry

explanation.surface: Steering clear of family in a crowded place, with no great rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'relations' means sexual relations, not relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence from sexual relations is the virtue of purity.

clue.text: Antiquated writer, nearly on time, stood still

parts.note: to stand for office is to run, so stood gives ran

indicators.note: nearly the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a quill was an old-fashioned feather pen

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned author, almost punctual, stood motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a calm, peaceful scene is still.

clue.text: Iron Lady felt accoutrement

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, felt something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' reads as Thatcher's nickname but splits into FE and a girl's name; 'felt' is the fabric, not a past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft hat made of felt with a creased crown, worn as an accessory.

clue.text: Mouths laughing noisily in sport

parts.note: trap is slang for mouth
hooting is loud laughter

explanation.surface: Mouths guffawing at a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay-pigeon shooting at targets flung from a trap is a shooting sport.

clue.text: What bird's brought back as an offering

indicators.note: the pieces are brought back, read from end to start

parts.note: eh? is an informal what?
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a bird has returned as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or income given to the church as a contribution.

clue.text: A garment jockeys ultimately knit for nag

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters of a garment are shifted about
the last letter of knit is taken

explanation.surface: Racing jockeys finally knit a garment for their horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockeys' and 'nag' suggest horse racing, but nag is a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewish, scolding woman, one who harangues.

clue.text: Crook I detect pinching crockery is keen to have it

indicators.note: the crook, I and detect together pinch, or grip, the crockery in their middle

parts.note: to con is to swindle, as a crook does
to scent is to detect by smell
a cup is an item of crockery

explanation.surface: A villain says the detective spots him stealing china he covets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the slang for sex, so the definition is about lust.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustful or eager for sexual relations, 'it' being the euphemism.

clue.text: Buyer tours empty units one keeps stocking up

indicators.note: the buyer goes round, or tours, the other piece

parts.note: a spender is someone who buys

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, units leaves its outer letters

explanation.surface: A shopper visits bare depots while one keeps restocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking up' sounds like replenishing, but it means holding a stocking up.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter that holds a woman's stocking up on the leg.

clue.text: Jeer welcomes Head of Harrow in comprehensive

indicators.note: the jeer takes in its guest, holding it inside

parts.note: a catcall is a derisive whistle or shout

indicators.note: the first letter of Harrow is used

explanation.surface: Booing greets the Head of Harrow, an English public school, at a comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Covering everything, as a blanket clause meant to include all cases.

clue.text: Desire to receive family member's agreement

indicators.note: the desire word opens to take in the relative

parts.note: to covet is to desire
nan is a grandmother

explanation.surface: Wanting to welcome a relative's consent.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal binding pact or contract.

clue.text: First class mail: a fellow's put in guy's address

parts.note: A is first class, as in A1 or an A grade
post is mail

indicators.note: the fellow's word is put inside the rope

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to steady a tent
belonging to a man is his

explanation.surface: A first-class letter with a man's message placed in another man's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is not a man but a tent rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak to someone absent or abstract in a rhetorical aside, addressing them directly.

clue.text: Put down journalist holding printed work up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the journalist holds the book inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone humbled a reporter for holding up publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce someone in rank is to downgrade them.

clue.text: Plant borders in mainly radiant landscape

indicators.note: the borders are the outer letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A plant growing round the edges of a sunny landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Soccer pitches around the side get noisier

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the side
to pitch is to toss, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: an end is a side or extremity

explanation.surface: Football grounds around the stand become louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitches' looks like football fields but it is the anagram signal, making CRESCO around END.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to build gradually in volume, like the musical direction.

clue.text: Man in Genesis covering Queen or The Stones?

indicators.note: the man covers, or encloses, the queen

parts.note: Cain is the son of Adam in the Book of Genesis
R, for Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: Is the Bible man covering Queen or the Rolling Stones?
explanation.walkthrough: The rock bands Genesis, Queen and the Stones are red herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of stones heaped as a marker or memorial.

clue.text: Rival soldiers retreating in case of emergency

indicators.note: the reversed soldiers go in the case
the case is the outer letters of emergency
the soldiers go backwards, so their word reads in reverse

parts.note: men are soldiers

explanation.surface: An opposing force's troops pulling back in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an opponent or foe.

clue.text: Several Asian countries rating boring stage number

indicators.note: the rating bores into the song, going inside it

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: Several Asian nations rating a stage song dull.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holds Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman and others, so it spans several nations.

clue.text: Thus doctor's about to crack clue, the last

indicators.note: the reversed pair is set to break into the clue word

parts.note: a hint is a clue

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: so means thus
MD is a doctor of medicine; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: So the doctor is about to solve a clue, the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SO MD to DMOS, which cracks HINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Farthest behind, so the last of all.

clue.text: Religious text books, unspecified ones

parts.note: lit is short for literature, books
any refers to unspecified ones

explanation.surface: A religious text from some books, which ones not stated.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of petitions recited in church worship.

clue.text: Afflict one woman after a lot of hassle

indicators.note: the one woman comes after the first piece
most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: aggro is British slang for trouble or hassle
I is the Roman numeral one
Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: A woman afflicted after a lot of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause distress or grief, to trouble someone.
